title: MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation
summary: Scaling deep learning recommendation models is an effective way to improve model expressiveness. Existing approaches often incur substantial computational overhead, making them difficult to deploy in large-scale industrial systems under strict latency constraints. Recent sparse activation scaling methods, such as Sparse Mixture-of-Experts, reduce computation by activating only a subset of parameters, but still suffer from high memory access costs and limited personalization capacity due to the large size and small number of experts. To address these challenges, we propose MSN, a memory-based sparse activation scaling framework for recommendation models. MSN dynamically retrieves personalized representations from a large parameterized memory and integrates them into downstream feature interaction modules via a memory gating mechanism, enabling fine-grained personalization with low computational overhead. To enable further expansion of the memory capacity while keeping both computational and memory access costs under control, MSN adopts a Product-Key Memory (PKM) mechanism, which factorizes the memory retrieval complexity from linear time to sub-linear complexity. In addition, normalization and over-parameterization techniques are introduced to maintain balanced memory utilization and prevent memory retrieval collapse. We further design customized Sparse-Gather operator and adopt the AirTopK operator to improve training and inference efficiency in industrial settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MSN consistently improves recommendation performance while maintaining high efficiency. Moreover, MSN has been successfully deployed in the Douyin Search Ranking System, achieving significant gains over deployed state-of-the-art models in both offline evaluation metrics and large-scale online A/B test.

title: TokenFormer V2: Breaking the Resolution-Complexity Dilemma in Unified Recommendation
summary: Industrial recommendation faces a resolution--complexity dilemma: dense interactions make detailed modeling of long behavior histories expensive, while compact history summaries restrict the evidence available to prediction. A unified backbone must preserve rich behavioral details within strict serving budgets. We introduce \textbf{TokenFormer V2}, a unified architecture that explicitly decouples \emph{representation resolution} from \emph{interaction density}. Its group-wise token layout jointly encodes behavior segments with non-sequential context, expands interaction ranges via hierarchical group merging, and coordinates distributed groups through \emph{NS Fusion} and \emph{Global Sync} modules. Through this \emph{local--global decomposition} paradigm, computation is concentrated on structured interactions while preserving fine-grained evidence, ensuring that every encoded event remains directly accessible to the \emph{Full-Resolution Readout} module. On the Tencent Advertising Algorithm Competition 2026 (TAAC 2026) benchmark, TokenFormer V2 achieves top-ranking accuracy among unified recommendation baselines while using \textbf{5.1$\times$ fewer FLOPs} than leading baselines, sustaining its advantage across long histories and imbalanced behavior domains. Furthermore, in billion-parameter evaluations on WeChat Channels advertising, it consistently outperforms state-of-the-art industrial baselines, yielding up to a \textbf{+0.07 pp} overall AUC gain. In live online A/B testing against the production model, TokenFormer V2 delivers a statistically significant \textbf{2.33\% increase in GMV}. These results establish TokenFormer V2 as a battle-tested blueprint for scalable, full-resolution behavior modeling in industrial recommendation.

title: CLEAR: Legible and Steerable Recommendation via Grounded Natural-Language Interests
summary: Modern recommenders keep learned preferences in representations people cannot inspect or change. We present CLEAR (Controllable and Legible End-to-end Architecture for Recommendation), an end-to-end system deployed at Meta and built around an editable natural-language interest layer. CLEAR makes a ranked subset of inferred interests readable and stores accepted additions and suppressions as authoritative preference state. Behavioral grounding maps each inferred interest back to supporting events in the user's own history. The resulting interest object is also a serving address: its label and profile-conditioned rewrites drive lexical retrieval, its supporting events seed behavioral retrieval, its projection queries an embedding index, and its stable identity supports ranking, attribution, and exposure control. A fresh user declaration may precede behavioral support, so it enters through the same serving identity and initially draws candidates from topical retrieval. Ranking makes those candidates competitive, while a delivery controller observes attributable exposure and replenishes underexposed interests. Direct user review found that users rated about 88.5% of displayed interests accurate. In an offline benchmark using a shared evaluation protocol, the Specialized 3B generator reached 0.3967 mean-user F1@10, compared with 0.3633 for Gemini 2.5 Pro and 0.1911 for the prior generator. For a newly declared interest, a user-randomized cumulative ablation measured same-day delivery losses of 8.7 percentage points for added-interest ranking terms, 11.1 for reserved top-slot insertion, and 13.7 for interest-conditioned candidate sourcing, conditional on the tested removal sequence. CLEAR components have operated in production for over one year; the system spans four surfaces on Instagram and Facebook, with an interest layer people can inspect, correct, and use to direct recommendations.

title: CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer
summary: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction is fundamental to online advertising systems. While Deep Learning Recommendation Models (DLRMs) with explicit feature interactions have long dominated this domain, recent advances in generative recommenders have shown promising results in content recommendation. However, adapting these transformer-based architectures to ads CTR prediction still presents unique challenges, including handling post-scoring contextual signals, maintaining offline-online consistency, and scaling to industrial workloads. We present CADET (Context-Conditioned Ads Decoder-Only Transformer), an end-to-end decoder-only transformer for ads CTR prediction deployed at LinkedIn. Our approach introduces several key innovations: (1) a context-conditioned decoding architecture with multi-tower prediction heads that explicitly model post-scoring signals such as ad position, resolving the chicken-and-egg problem between predicted CTR and ranking; (2) a self-gated attention mechanism that stabilizes training by adaptively regulating information flow at both representation and interaction levels; (3) a timestamp-based variant of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) that captures temporal relationships across timescales from seconds to months; (4) session masking strategies that prevent the model from learning dependencies on unavailable in-session events, addressing train-serve skew; and (5) production engineering techniques including tensor packing, sequence chunking, and custom Flash Attention kernels that enable efficient training and serving at scale. In online A/B testing, CADET achieves a 11.04\% CTR lift compared to the production LiRank baseline model, a hybrid ensemble of DCNv2 and sequential encoders. The system has been successfully deployed on LinkedIn's advertising platform, serving the main traffic for homefeed sponsored updates.

title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as recommenders in e-commerce and conversational shopping systems, where they select a product from a set of retrieved candidates described in natural language. Their decisions should depend on relevance to the user query, but may also be influenced by surface-level properties of the descriptions, such as their length. Detecting such structural biases is difficult because relevance labels are rarely available. We propose a label-free framework to audit LLM-based recommender systems for structural bias. Candidate descriptions are rewritten by randomly assigned paraphrasing models and presented in random order. We prove that, if the recommender's choice is invariant to these rewritings, every paraphraser is selected with equal probability, yielding a statistical test that requires no relevance labels. A four-step statistical pipeline tests this property and quantifies the contribution of each description feature while controlling for query-product relevance. We apply the framework to verbosity bias on 20{,}000 product queries and nine recommender LLMs from five model families. After controlling for the measured relevance signals, description length has a positive effect on selection in all nine models, increasing the odds of selection by up to 38% per standard deviation of length. Relevance remains the primary driver of recommendations, while verbosity acts as a consistent secondary signal whose strength depends on the model family. Since the framework needs only black-box access and no annotations, it can be run as a routine audit of deployed shopping assistants, and we provide an auditing protocol with cost and sample-size guidance.

title: The Revenue Cost of Inference in Online Assortment Optimization
summary: A seller running an assortment experiment must earn revenue while collecting data to compare future offers. For a regular finite-dimensional parametric choice model and a finite assortment family, we characterize the oracle frontier between expected revenue loss and the largest local first-order variance constant across prespecified revenue comparisons. The oracle benchmark remains finite at zero cost exactly when revenue-maximizing assortments provide information in every target-gradient direction. When costly offers can supply the missing information, we derive the exact leading coefficient of the inverse-budget variance law and the limiting optimal spending shares. A pilot-based procedure reserves reference offers to preserve information and tightens the estimated budget constraint to account for uncertainty. We give conditions for the implemented design's variance criterion to converge to the stabilized oracle value at a fixed budget and reference share. Simulations with synthetic instances and Expedia-calibrated markets show that allocating offers across the full assortment family can improve the precision of revenue comparisons under a common opportunity-cost budget. Additional experiments assess pilot spending, budget protection, and sensitivity to choice-model misspecification.

title: Beyond Similarity: Heterogeneous Graph Learning for Multi-Objective Food Substitution in Charitable Food Agencies
summary: Charitable food agencies play an important role in alleviating food insecurity by distributing donated food to people in need. However, they rely on ad hoc in-kind donations and often face shortages of specific foods, so they offer substitutes. A good food substitution requires matching household preferences, nutritional needs, and item similarity. Agencies have limited direct records of consumption behavior due to resource constraints, making it challenging to make an appropriate substitution decision that meets multiple criteria. In this study, we propose a heterogeneous graph neural network (HeteroGNN), a source-grounded recommendation framework for food substitution in charitable food agencies. We first build a unified relational graph from large-scale public data sources, combining household behavior on food consumption and food nutrient information in the United States (US) context. We treat the substitution recommendation as a multi-objective ranking problem with three targets, including behavior affinity, health suitability, and substitution similarity. We train and validate the proposed framework under standard graph relationship and adverse cold-start settings by removing relational edges from the graph. Our results show that the proposed framework leverages relational information beyond node features in predicting consumption behavior. Additionally, the proposed framework remains robust with sparsity when the model receives incomplete information about behavior and nutrient features. Finally, we show the weak correlation among different objectives, thereby justifying the multi-objective framing as a replacement for an aggregated decision. The proposed framework can help downstream charitable agency decision-makers make contextspecific substitution recommendations with limited information available.

title: Intrinsic Attention as Navigator: A Non-Generative Retrieval Method for Multi-Hop Queries
summary: For multi-hop queries in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), it is crucial to accurately obtain evidence pieces. In this study, we propose a training-free method for multi-hop query retrieval, named Intrinsic Navigating-based Non-Generative Retrieval (IN-Retriever). Instead of generating intermediate reasoning text, the method extracts the bridging clue from the internal attention of the embedding model based on the current context and retrieved candidate documents. During iterative clue extraction and document retrieval, IN-Retriever strips away revealed clues from the embedded query vector and then reranks candidate documents in a targeted manner, thereby steering retrieval toward hidden next-hop evidence. In the experiments, we confirm the feasibility and effectiveness of using intrinsic attention signals to guide external multi-hop retrieval. Experimental results show that our method precisely collects sufficient documents to support multi-hop queries and significantly outperforms sparse and dense retrieval methods.

title: Benchmarking Multi-Modal Graph-based Social Media Popularity Prediction
summary: Social media popularity prediction aims to forecast the future reach or influence of online content from early-stage observations. Accurate prediction enables key downstream applications, such as advertising optimization and strategic content planning by users, creators, and platforms. Despite substantial progress, existing popularity prediction works often fail to jointly consider multimodal content and temporal social interaction signals. Moreover, the literature remains highly fragmented across datasets, modalities, observation windows, prediction targets, and evaluation protocols. This fragmentation prevents fair comparison and obscures a systematic understanding of how textual, visual, temporal, and interaction-based signals jointly shape popularity dynamics. To address these challenges, we introduce MMG-Pop, a Multi-modal Graph-based Popularity Prediction benchmark, which unifies datasets, modalities, temporal interaction signals, and representative baselines under a standardized evaluation protocol. Furthermore, we propose MMG-PopNet, a unified multi-modal graph-based network that jointly models the aforementioned multi-modal signals and graph-structured social interactions. Extensive experiments on MMG-Pop across Bluesky and Reddit platforms demonstrate the superior performance of MMG-PopNet and yield new insights into cross-platform training generalization, multi-task prediction benefits, multi-modality contributions, and LLM prediction limitations. These findings establish a foundation for future research on social dynamics modeling and intervention under heterogeneous modalities and socially-aware agentic ecosystem paradigms.

title: LMEG-Doc: Layout-Grounded Multi-View Evidence Graphs for Multimodal Long-Document Retrieval
summary: Retrieving relevant evidence from multimodal long documents remains challenging, as supporting information is often distributed across different pages and modalities. Existing retrieval methods primarily rank document elements by their individual similarity to a question, often overlooking relationships among complementary evidence. Consequently, relevant figures and tables may receive low retrieval scores even when they contain essential information. To address this limitation, we introduce LMEG-Doc, a layout-grounded multi-view evidence graph framework for multimodal long-document retrieval. We first construct an evidence graph that captures structural and contextual relationships among document elements, and introduce Cross-Page Relation Refinement (CRR) to discover additional connections across distant pages through VLM-based verification. Building on this graph, we combine multimodal retrieval signals with graph-guided relevance propagation to recover connected supporting evidence at both layout and page levels. Experiments on MMDocIR, DocScope, and FinRAGBench-V demonstrate consistent retrieval improvements, including outperforming retrievers fine-tuned on MMDocIR without task-specific training. Furthermore, augmenting existing question-answering pipelines with our retrieved evidence improves answer accuracy by 7.6% on DocScope and 15.8% on FinRAGBench-V, demonstrating the effectiveness of relationship-aware multimodal retrieval.

title: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
summary: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to use an external Zoom-in tool for fine-grained visual search. Recent works employ supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) with tool-specific designs to enable such capabilities. However, achieving logical reasoning alongside accurate and efficient tool use remains a significant challenge. To address this, we shift the focus away from increasing RL complexity and instead identify SFT data quality as a key bottleneck. We then propose LogT (short for Logically Think with Images), a fully automated SFT data engine that explicitly enforces logic-chain-guided reasoning. LogT generates an SFT dataset featuring challenging, visually grounded questions and structured tool-use traces with human-like logic. We validate our approach by fine-tuning two base models, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B, on the dataset and evaluating them across seven benchmark test sets. We show that LogT-SFT based on Qwen2.5-VL-7B outperforms the state-of-the-art trained with both SFT and RL, despite using 3.1$\times$ less data and $>120\times$ fewer GPU hours. Furthermore, applying a simple RL recipe without tool-specific design on LogT-SFT yields a model that surpasses prior methods with complex RL setups by a substantial 9.59-point margin. In addition to strong performance gains, our model exhibits higher tool-use accuracy and efficiency, as well as more structured and logically consistent reasoning traces, directly validating the effectiveness of our approach.

title: jXBW: A Compressed Index Enabling Structure-Aware JSONL Retrieval for Structured RAG
summary: Providing structured information to large language models (LLMs) has been shown to improve multi-step reasoning and factual accuracy (e.g., StructRAG, ICLR 2025; RAS, ICLR 2026); recent retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems reconstruct structure from retrieved text on every query. When the corpus is already structured, as in JSON Lines (JSONL), used for LLM prompts, chemical compounds, and geospatial objects, this per-query rebuilding can be replaced by direct structural retrieval. Its core operation is substructure search: finding all JSON objects in a collection that contain a given query tree. Existing approaches index each object separately, so index space and query time grow with collection size; XML-based engines add conversion overhead and semantic mismatches. We propose jXBW, a compressed index for fast substructure search over JSONL, combining three innovations: (i) a merged tree representation that consolidates repeated structures across objects, (ii) a succinct tree encoding based on the eXtended Burrows-Wheeler Transform (XBW), and (iii) a three-phase substructure search algorithm on this encoding. Together they achieve query-dependent complexity in compressed space: the search avoids a full scan of the collection, and its cost grows with the numbers of candidate matches and results. Experiments on seven real-world datasets, including PubChem (1 million compounds) and OpenStreetMap (6.6 million objects), show that jXBW outperforms the strongest tree-based baseline by 16x on the smallest dataset and by up to 2,800x on the largest, while the XML-based engine Saxon does not complete the 1,000-query workload on PubChem within 24 hours. jXBW brings substructure search over million-object JSONL collections into the sub-millisecond range.

title: CURATOR: Scalable Fine-grained Evidence Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Decision Models
summary:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) provides entire retrieved passages to the LLM, even though only a handful of spans within them contain the evidence pertaining to the question. While precise selection of these spans can improve context utilization, identifying them in isolation is challenging. A span may appear irrelevant by itself, and deciding whether to retain it may require examining other retrieved information. One can evaluate each span's candidacy with the full retrieved context, but this is computationally inefficient as the same text must be processed repeatedly. Pretrained decision model can be used to efficiently evaluate multiple spans simultaneously, allowing each decision to consider the surrounding spans as well. However, our experiments show that their ability to identify relevant evidence deteriorates as the number of simultaneous decisions increases.
  To address this, we introduce CURATOR, a fine-tuned decision model trained to make reliable evidence-selection decisions over large candidate sets. By training a decision model to select varying numbers of supporting spans from large candidate pools, CURATOR develops the capability to select evidence for RAG while retaining the computational efficiency of joint decision-making. We observe that CURATOR maintains a strong evidence discrimination capability as the number of candidates increases, generalizes across different tasks and document domains, and improves downstream RAG performance, particularly when the available context is limited.
